children.text: Stretching about 9 km along both banks of the Iloilo River in the heart of Iloilo City, this is the longest linear park in the Philippines. Walk for free past mangrove trails, sunrises and sunsets over the water, the old port of Muelle Loney and riverside restaurant strips, and see everyday life in Iloilo up close.

The Iloilo River Esplanade is a riverside park along both banks of the Iloilo River, which flows east to west through the middle of Iloilo City, and is considered the longest linear park in the Philippines. Its sections add up to about
9 km

, from Carpenter Bridge upstream to Drilon Bridge and the fast craft terminal downstream, and 11 bridges tie together the riverbanks of five districts: Molo, Mandurriao, La Paz, Lapuz and City Proper. There is no admission fee, and brick walkways, palm trees, mangrove forests and viewing decks follow one another along the way.
The site began as a dike road built to hold back floods. The first section (Esplanade 1, about
1.2 km
), designed by landscape architect Paulo Alcazaren, opened on
August 18, 2012
, and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) added sections one after another from
to reach today's length. In

, Esplanade 11 in Lapuz near the river mouth and the riverside promenade on Sunset Boulevard upstream opened. The river development project won the Galing Pook Award for excellence in local governance in
, and the esplanade received the Asian Townscape Award, given by UN-Habitat's Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific and other partners, in

The Iloilo River is an estuary where seawater moves in and out with the tides, and its banks are said to support more than twenty of the mangrove species that grow in the Philippines. Mangrove forest reaches right up to the walkway, so you can spot waterbirds and fish in the middle of the city. The construction drew criticism for damaging mangroves, and since then the city government, businesses and schools have kept replanting mangroves along the banks together.

Joggers out before dawn, people dancing Zumba, and couples and families photographing the sunset make up daily life here. Esplanade 1 sits next to a riverside restaurant strip and Mandurriao's restaurant and bar streets, so a walk can roll straight into dinner. It suits travelers who want to spend half a day walking between city sights, families looking for a free place to relax with children, and expats and long-stay visitors based in Iloilo.

blocks.title: Esplanade 1 — Carpenter Bridge to Iloilo Bridge

children.text: The signature section, about
long and first opened in

, follows the Mandurriao bank on a brick path lined with palms and flowering trees. A large esplanade sign marks the entrance by Iloilo Bridge on Diversion Road, and Esplanade 2 runs parallel on the opposite Molo bank.

blocks.title: Datu Paiburong statue and Dinagyang warrior mural

children.text: At the Esplanade 1 entrance stands a statue of Datu Paiburong, who in legend ruled the land of Iloilo (Irong-Irong), holding a spear and shield, and the wall beside it carries a relief mural of Dinagyang festival warriors. Many historians regard the Maragtas, the source of the legend, as a story written in the early 20th century.

blocks.title: Sunrise and sunset over the river

children.text: Because the river runs east to west, you can watch the sun rise and set over the water from the bridges or the banks. Depending on the season, the sun rises between
and sets between
. The giant letter sculpture on the riverside plaza is a popular photo spot.

Mangroves form forests along the banks around Tabucan, La Paz and Muelle Loney. At high tide the roots are underwater, at low tide the mudflats are exposed, and waterbirds such as night herons often perch in the branches.

This riverside flower garden in Nabitasan, La Paz district, has a flower path lined with colorful heart arches and a koi pond. It was created as part of a city beautification project, is listed as open free of charge
, and is a favorite spot for family photos.

blocks.title: Muelle Loney and the Philippine Maritime Museum

children.text: Esplanade 8, downstream on the City Proper side, follows Muelle Loney, the old port that opened to international trade in the
mid-19th century
. The ground floor of the neoclassical customs house, built during the American period, holds the Philippine Maritime Museum, opened by the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) in
January 2023
, which you can visit free of charge Tuesday to Sunday,
This four-lane road of about
5 km
, opened in
January 2025
, follows the river from Mandurriao to Cabanbang in Oton. It has a riverside promenade of about

blocks.title: Riverside restaurant strip and food streets

children.text: Riverside Boardwalk on Diversion Road, next to Esplanade 1, gathers restaurants and pubs overlooking the river. Across the road, Smallville Complex stays busy with restaurants and bars until late at night, and a little farther north are the restaurant streets of Atria Park District and Festive Walk Parade.

The museum is closed on Mondays, so on a Monday limit yourself to the walk along the Muelle Loney bank. Many sections lack shade, so it is best to wrap up the morning before

Enter a large landmark as your destination, such as "Riverside Boardwalk" for Esplanade 1, "Iloilo City Garden of Love" for the Garden of Love or "Iloilo Customs House" for Esplanade 8, so you don't miss your driver.
The fast craft from Bacolod takes about

Sailings are canceled in bad weather, so check the operator's schedule announcements before you set out.

The north bank (Esplanades 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 and the Lapuz section) and the south bank (Esplanades 2, 4, 6, 10 and 8) are linked by bridges. Walking one bank from Carpenter Bridge upstream to the downstream end covers about
and takes
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours
at an easy pace, so it is easier to walk one way and call a Grab for the return.
Whether bikes are allowed differs by section, so follow the signs. Diversion Road and Sunset Boulevard have bike lanes.

, and when heavy rain coincides with high tide, the river rises and low-lying areas such as La Paz can flood. The riverside is pleasant on clear mornings after rain, but put off walking the banks on days when warnings are issued.

If you want to walk the esplanade often, staying in Mandurriao's new city center near Esplanade 1 is convenient. Business and mid-range hotels cluster around Smallville Complex, Atria Park District and Iloilo Business Park,
5–25 minutes
on foot from the riverbank. For an old-town atmosphere, stay in City Proper near Calle Real and Muelle Loney and walk the downstream sections. Mid-range hotels cost about
a night, and during Dinagyang rates rise and rooms fill up early.

After your walk, choose from Philippine chain restaurants to cafés and bars at Riverside Boardwalk next to Esplanade 1, Smallville Complex, Atria Park District and Festive Walk Parade, which runs about
1.1 km
. Shops change often, so pick whatever is open when you are there.

While in Iloilo, try La Paz batchoy, noodles topped with pork offal and crispy pork cracklings; pancit Molo, a clear soup with shrimp and pork dumplings; and chicken inasal grilled over charcoal. Batchoy costs about
a bowl at the long-running stalls of La Paz Market, a little over
10 minutes
by car from the Esplanade 1 entrance, and Madge Café in the same market has brewed coffee through cloth filters since
Watch the sunrise from a bank facing downstream and the sunset from a bank facing upstream toward Carpenter Bridge to capture the light reflected on the water.
The banks have little shade at midday. Bring a hat and water, and rest indoors from
10:00 AM to 3:00 PM

Section numbers do not run in order along the river but alternate between the two banks. Before you walk, check names such as "Esplanade 1" and "Esplanade 8" in a map app and decide which bridges to cross so you don't get lost.
Walking one bank end to end is about
. Walk one way only and take a Grab or jeepney back to save your energy.
Whether bikes are allowed differs by section, so check the signs at the entrances. A facility with showers and bike storage is being built in
at the skate park north of Iloilo Bridge.
The Philippine Maritime Museum is closed on Mondays and open Tuesday to Sunday,
. Hours may change, so check the latest notices from the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP).
Mosquitoes are plentiful near the mangroves around dusk. Bring insect repellent for evening walks.

In the rainy season and during typhoons, the Iloilo River can rise quickly, and when heavy rain coincides with high tide, the banks and nearby low-lying areas can flood. If a weather warning is issued, put off your riverside walk and check the latest announcements from Iloilo City. Some sections may be temporarily closed for connection works and construction of facilities.
The Iloilo River is a tidal estuary, so its currents and water level change during the day. Do not climb down to the water beyond the railings or go into the river.
At night, stick mainly to Esplanade 1, which is well lit and busy, and do not walk alone late on quiet sections.
Weekend evenings and the Dinagyang period draw big crowds. Watch out for pickpockets and keep your phone and wallet in front of you.
Littering and smoking are penalized under city ordinances. Since
February 2025
, Sunset Boulevard has banned unauthorized vendors and staged photo shoots.
Do not break mangrove branches or go into the forest. Mangroves are protected, and it is easy to sink into the mudflats.
